editorApprovedScope.requiredReaderDisclosure: By explicit editorial approval, this assessment scores only Randal Rauser and Dan Barker in the main discussion (approximately 1:52–1:28:28) and closing remarks (2:00:08–2:03:18). This is an informal discussion, not a debate with timed formal rounds. Cameron Bertuzzi contributes arguments as unscored context; only the debaters’ own contributions and replies receive assessment, and no moderator argument is credited to either side. Unequal prompting is considered when evaluating opportunities to respond. Introductions, audience Q&A and the outro are excluded, with no credit, penalty, inferred concession or failure-to-reply inference from that material. Rauser’s closing reference to an excluded audience exchange cannot support criticism of Barker’s assessed performance. Public automatic captions were supplemented by targeted automated audio checks; these were not direct human listening.
editorApprovedScope.scopeInterpretation: Rauser defends the Christian God’s worship-worthiness through contextual and canonical reading; Barker challenges that worthiness through moral depictions and failed communication. Do not convert the motion into whether God exists, treat Rauser as defending every surveyed Christian interpretation, or impose on Barker a positive alternative theology.
